main_indications: Emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose using an FDA-labeled OTC naloxone product

refill.summary: An FDA-labeled OTC naloxone package is sold as a nonprescription product; prescription-refill rules do not create a refill requirement for the OTC package.

transfer.summary: An OTC naloxone package is not transferred as a prescription merely because prescription naloxone products also exist.

partial_fill.summary: Prescription partial-fill rules do not govern an ordinary sale of an intact FDA-labeled OTC naloxone package.

masspat.summary: Ordinary OTC naloxone sales are not MassPAT dispensing transactions.

quantity_limit.summary: The OTC package follows its retail labeling and applicable general retail law, not Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription quantity rules.

authorities.name: Massachusetts DCP OTC naloxone advisory
authorities.section: OTC naloxone outside DCP controlled-substance regulations

verification_notes: FDA-labeled OTC naloxone is a separate product category from prescription naloxone under current Massachusetts DCP guidance; checked 2026-08-14.
